overview: White develops the knight instead of choosing a named French line and waits to see Black's set-up. Most games go 3...Nf6 or 3...c5 and transpose into a Classical, Advance or Tarrasch-type French. The gambit tries (3...dxe4 followed by a knight sortie) are rare sidelines.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3 or Bd3 and transpose into a standard French structure.
Push e5 to gain space and aim at a kingside attack.

black_ideas.idea: Attack the d4 base with ...c5 and ...Nc6.
Solve the light-squared bishop by ...b6/...Ba6 or an exchange.

typical_structures.structure: French chain pawns on d4/e5 against d5/e6 after 3...Nf6 4.e5.
Tension in the centre with ...dxe4 and Nc3 transpositions.

character.notes: Main line transposes to ordinary French play: slow, manoeuvring, with Black cramped but sound.

gambit.notes: No material changes hands in the position or the usual 3...Nf6 / 3...c5 replies; the named gambit is a rare 3...dxe4 sideline.

soundness.notes: 3.Nf3 is a sound developing move; nothing is risked in the main replies.

structure.notes: Semi-open like the French in general: Black attacks d4 with ...c5 on a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: A standard if uncommon move order; not an offbeat line in itself.

level.notes: Usual French plans, little theory to memorise.

sublines_that_differ.name: Gambit sidelines
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives a pawn for quick development and piece activity; rare and unclear from memory.

character.reason: Transposes to French play that is neither forcing nor especially hard to crack.

gambit.reason: The usual replies keep material level; only a rare 3...dxe4 line is gambit-like.

soundness.reason: 3.Nf3 risks nothing in the main lines.

structure.reason: French centre with Black pressing d4 down the half-open c-file.

approach.reason: A plain developing move order, not played purely for surprise.

level.reason: Ordinary French plans with little to memorise.

plans.reason: Too undefined to pin to a plan.
